# Research Question

Do colleges with higher tuition rates have higher graduation rates?

For my final project, I want to investigate whether there is a relationship between college tuition costs and graduation rates in the United States.

I am interested in whether students attending more expensive colleges are more likely to graduate than students attending less expensive colleges.

# Hypotheses

My hypothesis is that colleges with higher tuition rates will generally have higher graduation rates.

# Data Source

I plan to use the U.S. Department of Education's College Scorecard dataset.

Data website:
https://collegescorecard.ed.gov/data/

Documentation:
https://collegescorecard.ed.gov/data/data-documentation/

The College Scorecard contains institution-level information about colleges in the United States, including tuition, graduation rates, enrollment, and institutional characteristics.

I will begin with the most recent institution-level data and investigate which academic years are represented by my selected variables.

```{r}

install.packages("tidyverse")

```

```{r}
college_data <- read.csv("Most-Recent-Cohorts-Institution.csv")
```


```{r}

# Select your original College Scorecard file
file_path <- file.choose()

# Read only the first row to get column names
column_names <- names(read.csv(file_path, nrows = 1))

# Choose the columns needed for the project
keep_columns <- c(
  "UNITID",
  "INSTNM",
  "STABBR",
  "CONTROL",
  "PREDDEG",
  "HIGHDEG",
  "TUITIONFEE_IN",
  "TUITIONFEE_OUT",
  "C150_4",
  "UGDS",
  "ADM_RATE"
)

# Skip all other columns
column_types <- ifelse(
  column_names %in% keep_columns,
  NA,
  "NULL"
)

# Load only the selected columns
college_data <- read.csv(
  file_path,
  colClasses = column_types,
  na.strings = c("NA", "NULL", "PS", "")
)

# Check that the data loaded
dim(college_data)
head(college_data)

```


```{r}
write.csv(
  college_data,
  "college_data.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)

# Check its size in MB
file.info("college_data.csv")$size / 1024^2

```

```{r}

## Important Variables

My smaller dataset contains 11 columns. Each row represents one college or institution.

The most important columns for my research are:

- UNITID: Unique identification number for each institution.
- INSTNM: Name of the college or university.
- STABBR: State where the institution is located.
- CONTROL: Whether the institution is public, private nonprofit, or private for-profit.
- PREDDEG: Predominant degree offered by the institution.
- HIGHDEG: Highest degree offered by the institution.
- TUITIONFEE_IN: In-state tuition and required fees.
- TUITIONFEE_OUT: Out-of-state tuition and required fees.
- C150_4: Graduation rate for four-year degrees within 150% of normal time, generally six years.
- UGDS: Undergraduate enrollment.
- ADM_RATE: Admission rate.

The two most important variables for my research are TUITIONFEE_IN and C150_4 because they allow me to compare tuition costs and graduation rates.

CONTROL is also important because I want to examine whether public and private institutions have different patterns.

ADM_RATE and UGDS may help explain why graduation rates differ between colleges.

I will likely focus on four-year institutions because graduation rates are measured differently for different types of schools.
```
